respect.name: Respect
respect.description: Thinking about other people's opinions, boundaries and rights.
respect.growth: Next time, try asking before you help. It shows you respect a person's choices.

understanding.name: Understanding
understanding.description: Trying to understand another person's situation.
understanding.growth: Try asking “How do you feel?” — and listen to the whole answer before you reply.

kindness.name: Kindness
kindness.growth: Small actions count. A kind comment or a smile can change someone's day.

caring.name: Caring
caring.description: Offering help or support when someone needs it.
caring.growth: Notice who might need support, and offer help in a practical way.

compassion.name: Compassion
compassion.description: Understanding someone's situation and acting to help them.
compassion.growth: When someone is hurt, try to feel with them — and then do something to help.

achievements.name: Good Listener
achievements.text: Choose to listen and understand in Help Colin.

collectibles.name: Old Key
collectibles.text: The rusty key the robin found. It had been buried for ten years.

collectibles.name: Robin Feather
collectibles.text: A tiny red-brown feather. The robin was Mary's very first friend at the manor.

collectibles.name: Wild Rose
collectibles.text: A single rose that survived the long winter. Gardens wait patiently for someone to care.

collectibles.name: Book Page I
collectibles.text: “Might I have a bit of earth?” — Mary asks Mr. Craven for a small piece of land to make things grow.

collectibles.name: Book Page II
collectibles.text: “It's wick!” — Dickon shows Mary that a grey branch is still alive inside. Things that look dead can still grow.

collectibles.name: Book Page III
collectibles.text: “Where you tend a rose, my lad, a thistle cannot grow.” — When we grow good thoughts, there is less room for bad ones.

quotes: Every garden has a story. Every choice reveals something about us.
Things that look grey can still be alive inside.
A garden grows when someone cares for it.
Listening is the first seed of understanding.
